Why builders · Not a generic trades site

A builder's customer decides differently.

Someone booking a plumber wants it fixed today. Someone choosing a builder is about to hand over the biggest cheque of their life to a stranger. That takes a completely different site.

They research you for weeks

They will read every page you have, twice, and look at every photo. A one-page site runs out of things to say and they go and read your competitor instead.

They are frightened, not cheap

Everyone knows someone whose build went wrong. The site's job is to make you the safe choice, which is what the process, the licence and the finished jobs are doing there.

Photos do the closing

Nothing you write will beat eight good photos of a finished job in a suburb they recognise. That is why the gallery is not an afterthought stuck on the end.

Every service and every suburb gets its own page, because that is how someone searching finds you and how Google works out what you do and where.

Questions · From builders

What builders ask me.

I already get all my work through word of mouth. Why do I need a site?

Word of mouth still sends people to Google. Someone recommends you at a barbecue, the bloke looks you up on the drive home, finds nothing, and rings whoever does turn up. The site is not there to replace your referrals, it is there to stop them leaking.

I have a Facebook page. Is that enough?

It is something, but it is not yours and it does not show up when someone searches for a builder in your suburb. A Facebook page also cannot list your services, your areas, your licence and your jobs in a way Google can read and rank.

What sort of builder is this for?

New homes, renovations, extensions, custom builds, decks and pergolas, granny flats. If you quote jobs and you want more of the good ones, it works. It is aimed at builders doing solid work who are invisible online.

Do you show my licence number and insurance?

Yes, if you give them to me. I never invent a licence number, an ABN, an insurance status or a review. If I do not have it, the site does not claim it.

What if I do not have good photos?

Most builders have more than they think, sitting on their phone. Job photos taken on site are usually better than staged ones anyway, because they look real. We work with what you have and I will tell you straight if a job needs a couple more shots.

Do you work outside Newcastle?

Yes. I am based in Newcastle and most of my work is around the Hunter, but the build is done remotely, so where you are does not change the price or the timeline.
